latest_nl_proof:
Let K be an algebraic closure of k, and set J := I K[x_1,...,x_d] inside K[x_1,...,x_d]. The weighted grading and the homogeneity of I are not needed for the argument.

First handle the case d = 0. Then S = k. The affine 0-space over K has exactly one point, namely the origin. If I = S, then its zero locus is empty, contrary to the hypothesis that the zero locus is exactly the origin. Hence I = 0, so S/I is isomorphic to k, which is finite-dimensional over k.

Now assume d >= 1. The common zero locus of J in K^d is the same as the common zero locus of I in K^d: every element of I lies in J, and every element of J is a finite K[x_1,...,x_d]-linear combination of elements of I, so a point of K^d annihilates all elements of I if and only if it annihilates all elements of J. By hypothesis, V(J) = {0}.

Because K is algebraically closed, Hilbert's Nullstellensatz gives that the radical of J is the ideal of all polynomials vanishing on V(J). Since V(J) = {0}, this ideal is exactly (x_1,...,x_d). Therefore, for each i = 1,...,d, we have x_i in rad(J), so there exists an integer N_i >= 1 such that x_i^(N_i) belongs to J.

We next prove that J intersect S = I. The inclusion I subseteq J intersect S is immediate. For the reverse inclusion, let f be an element of J intersect S. Since f belongs to J, there exist finitely many elements g_1,...,g_m of I and polynomials A_1,...,A_m in K[x_1,...,x_d] such that
f = sum_{r=1}^m A_r g_r.
Let V be the finite-dimensional k-subspace of K spanned by 1 and by all coefficients of all the A_r. Choose a k-basis b_1,...,b_t of V with b_1 = 1. Since every coefficient of each A_r lies in V, we can write uniquely
A_r = sum_{s=1}^t b_s B_{r,s}
with B_{r,s} in S = k[x_1,...,x_d]. Hence
f = sum_{s=1}^t b_s G_s,
where G_s := sum_{r=1}^m B_{r,s} g_r belongs to I for each s.
Now set H_1 := G_1 - f and H_s := G_s for s > 1. Then each H_s lies in S, and
sum_{s=1}^t b_s H_s = 0
in K[x_1,...,x_d]. Write each H_s as a finite sum
H_s = sum_alpha c_{s,alpha} x^alpha
with c_{s,alpha} in k. Since the monomials x^alpha are linearly independent over K in the polynomial ring K[x_1,...,x_d], for each multi-index alpha we get
sum_{s=1}^t b_s c_{s,alpha} = 0
in K. But b_1,...,b_t are k-linearly independent, and each c_{s,alpha} lies in k. Therefore all c_{s,alpha} are zero. So every H_s is the zero polynomial. In particular H_1 = 0, hence f = G_1 belongs to I. This proves J intersect S = I.

Applying this to x_i^(N_i), we obtain x_i^(N_i) in I for every i. Therefore any monomial x_1^(a_1) ... x_d^(a_d) with some a_i >= N_i lies in I, because it is divisible by x_i^(N_i). It follows that the residue classes of the finitely many monomials x_1^(a_1) ... x_d^(a_d) with 0 <= a_i < N_i for all i span S/I over k. Hence S/I is finite-dimensional as a k-vector space.

Thus the lemma is proved.
role_in_parent: Turns the geometric conclusion of L3 into the finite-dimensional quotient needed for commutative-algebra arguments.
statement_nl: Let k be a field, let d be a nonnegative integer, let w_1,...,w_d be positive integers, and let S = k[x_1,...,x_d] with weighted grading deg(x_i)=w_i. Let I be a homogeneous ideal of S. If, over an algebraic closure of k, the common zero locus of I in affine d-space is exactly the origin, then S/I is finite-dimensional as a k-vector space.

domain_restrictions: d is a nonnegative integer (so affine d-space and the polynomial ring have d variables; includes the special case d = 0)
each weight w_i is a positive integer
I is homogeneous with respect to the weighted grading determined by deg(x_i) = w_i
the zero-locus condition is stated after base change to an algebraic closure of k, so points are taken in affine d-space over k_bar
statement_semantic_sketch.normalized_claim: For all fields k, all nonnegative integers d, all positive integer weights w_1 through w_d, and all ideals I in S = k[x_1,...,x_d] that are homogeneous for the weighted grading, if the variety over an algebraic closure k_bar has common zeros exactly at the origin in affine d-space, then the quotient ring S/I has finite dimension as a vector space over k.
quantifier_order: for all positive integer weights w_1,...,w_d
for all weighted-homogeneous ideals I of S = k[x_1,...,x_d]
if over k_bar the common zero locus of I in affine d-space equals exactly the origin
then S divided by I is finite-dimensional as a k-vector space
